messages:
marie_cs: FYI team — weekly account health snapshot for AcmePay. Seeing an error spike this week, want to coordinate triage and customer comms. Overall error rate 2.3% (baseline ~0.6%).

marie_cs: Quick breakdown: 5xx = 1.8% (majority 502/503), timeouts = 0.3%, rate-limited 0.2%. p95 latency up from 420ms -> 1.1s for this account. Spend is steady. Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/acmepay/errors

marie_cs: Top failing endpoints (last 7d):
- /v1/generate — 5xx: 420 errors, spike on Tue 03:10-04:00 UTC
- /v1/embeddings — 5xx: 120 errors, intermittent
- /v1/chat/stream — timeouts: 80 events, mostly long-running streams
- /v1/rerank — 429: 60 events (burst from 12:00-12:30 UTC Mon)
- /v1/batch/embeddings — 503: 50 errors (batch job window)

alex_eng: I can take /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Initial guess: upstream model worker OOM / overload during long sequences. I'll pull nginx/proxy logs and model process metrics.

sam_sre: I started a trace for last 48h on AcmePay's requests. Early signal shows a cluster of 502s correlating with GPU node reboots in cluster-gpu-3. Put a watch on node churn.

marie_cs: thanks. Can you both check if KV cache misses increased too? Customer reported more re-runs which would explain cost but not the 502s.

alex_eng: good call — checking cache hit ratios now. Also adding a temporary fallback to a lower-memory model variant for AcmePay's dedicated pool to see if errors drop.

devon_onboard: I’ll message the AM and CS lead to prepare an internal note for the customer. If this becomes a service-impact incident we should offer a rollback to the previous model version.

alex_eng: found relevant nginx snippets:
```
502 "upstream prematurely closed connection" for /v1/generate from 10.2.3.45
503 "no live upstreams" during batch window
```

sam_sre: created incident INC-2026-321 and attached traces. Assigned to alex_eng and infra-oncall. Incident bot: <#incidents/INC-2026-321>.

devon_onboard: customer-facing note draft: "We observed increased 5xx errors affecting some generation and embedding calls this week due to transient GPU node instability. We're actively mitigating and will update within 4 hours." Thoughts? :thinking_face:

marie_cs: good draft. Add that we’ve applied a temporary fallback and are monitoring metrics; include estimated next update in 2 hours.

alex_eng: mitigation steps taken: scaled up pooling on dedicated cluster for AcmePay, forced model fallback for heavy sequences, and restarted 2 unstable GPU nodes. P95 for generate down to 580ms in the last 15m, 5xx rate for /v1/generate dropped ~75%.

sam_sre: adding a rule to alert on >0.5% 5xx for a single customer route to catch earlier next time.

devon_onboard: I'll send the updated note to the AM + PM and offer a short postmortem call if the customer requests.

marie_cs: perfect. Action items: alex -> deep diff logs + root cause (ETA 24h), sam -> alert tuning and incident doc, devon -> customer comms + scheduling. Re-check in 3 hours or sooner if alerts trigger. :thumbsup:

alex_eng: on it.

sam_sre: monitoring.

ops_bot: ticket INC-2026-321 updated: status=investigating, assignees=[alex_eng, sam_sre], severity=high.
